card.occupation: Kitchen assistant at a primary school (about 25 hours a week, term-time only, 9:30 to 2:30). She preps vegetables, serves at the hatch, washes up and cleans down the kitchen.
card.education_detail: Left school at 16 with GCSEs, including a 5 in English and a 4 in maths. She started a Level 2 Health and Social Care course at Luton college but left partway through when she fell pregnant at 19. She has since done a Level 2 Food Hygiene certificate through work and a free online first aid course.
card.household: Lives with her son Zayan, aged 5, in a two-bedroom housing association flat in the Farley Hill area. She's not in a relationship, and Zayan's dad sees him most weekends, mostly without drama. Her mum lives a ten-minute walk away and does school pick-ups when Sana's shifts run over.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Luton to a family of Pakistani (Mirpuri) heritage. Her grandparents came over in the 1960s. She is Muslim, wears a hijab, prays when she can and goes to the mosque mainly for Eid and family occasions. She speaks English day to day and understands Pahari and Urdu, though she answers her nani in English more than she'd like. Being a single mum did cause some talk among the wider family, but most of them have come round, and her mum has been solidly on her side.
card.professional_persona: Reliable and quietly hardworking. The cook likes her because she doesn't moan and she remembers which kids have allergies. She worries about getting things wrong and will double-check labels and temperatures. The hours suit her because they fit around school, even if the money doesn't stretch far.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks a lot, mostly the school run and into town, and occasionally goes to a women-only swim session at the leisure centre with her cousin. She watches the odd England match if family have it on.
card.arts_persona: Likes Pakistani dramas on YouTube, which she watches with her mum and sometimes cries at. She also watches reality TV like Love Island 'ironically' and listens to a mix of Bollywood, Punjabi tracks and whatever's on TikTok. She does henna for friends and family before weddings and Eid, and she's genuinely good at it.
card.travel_persona: Has been to Pakistan twice, once as a child and once at 17 for a cousin's wedding. Apart from that, it's day trips to London, Southend or a cousin's in Birmingham. She'd love to take Zayan somewhere hot for a holiday one day, maybe Turkey, but it feels a long way off money-wise.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks everyday food at home like daal, chicken curry, rice and roti, with fish fingers and pasta when Zayan's being fussy. She learned most of it from her mum but still rings her to ask about quantities. Her treats are a takeaway from a grill place on Dunstable Road and the occasional Nando's.
hobbies_and_interests: Henna designs, with an Instagram page she barely posts on
Taking Zayan to Wardown Park and the museum there
Scrolling TikTok for cleaning and budgeting tips
Online shopping she mostly doesn't follow through on
skills: Batch cooking on a tight budget
card.career_goals: She'd like to become a teaching assistant, since she sees them at school and thinks she'd be good at it. She has looked at a Level 3 course but is nervous about going back to studying and about fitting it in. She'd also like to do henna properly as a side business for weddings.
card.voice: Soft, friendly and fairly quick when she's comfortable, but a bit hesitant at the start. She has a general Luton and South East accent. She uses 'erm' a lot and 'kind of' or 'sort of' to soften opinions, and ends sentences with 'you know?' or 'yeah'. She calls the evening meal 'dinner'. She says 'sorry' a lot, often as a repair ('sorry, I mean...'), and laughs nervously after giving an opinion. Silence makes her uneasy, so she'll fill it with 'erm, I don't know if that makes sense' or ask whether she's answered properly.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase and quick. She often leaves out apostrophes ('dont', 'im') and doesn't use many commas. She'll use 'tbh' or 'idk' and the odd 'x' or 'lol' by habit, then delete it if it's a formal form. Answers are short unless the question is about her son.
card.with_strangers: Warm and polite but shy at first. She wants to be helpful and worries about saying the wrong thing. Once she's settled she's chatty, kind and easy to talk to, and she'll agree with people readily rather than argue.
small_things: Zayan's obsession with dinosaurs and Bluey
Being knackered after a shift and the school run
The price of nappies and now school shoes
What they served at lunch today and which kids wouldn't eat it
A drama she's watching with her mum
deeper_things: Feeling judged by some relatives and aunties for having Zayan without being married
Worrying about money and whether she's doing enough for Zayan
Wishing she'd finished her college course
Getting anxious at night and overthinking things
Not being sure she wants to get married, despite family hints
How much she relies on her mum, and worrying about her mum's health
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slightly low angle, framed from the chest up and a little off-centre to the left. Lit by a ceiling light and some grey daylight from a window to her right, so one side of her face is slightly brighter. She's a young South Asian woman with warm brown skin, dark brown eyes and neat eyebrows, wearing light makeup. She is smiling a little awkwardly with her lips closed, as if waiting for the call to start. She wears a dusky pink jersey hijab pinned under the chin and a black zip-up hoodie over a grey top, with no glasses. Behind her is a magnolia living-room wall with a framed Arabic calligraphy print and a small canvas photo of her and a young boy. To one side is a grey fabric sofa with a folded fleece blanket and a plastic dinosaur toy on the cushion, and a clothes airer with small school polo shirts is partly visible at the edge of the frame.
